what_its_for: This patch is used to relieve pain in a specific area of your skin. It is most commonly used for pain caused by nerve damage after shingles (a painful rash caused by the chickenpox virus). The medicine in the patch numbs the skin and the area underneath it to reduce pain.
how_to_take: Apply the patch directly to your most painful skin area. Before putting on the patch, make sure the skin is clean, dry, and not broken or irritated. Remove the clear plastic backing and press the sticky side firmly onto your skin. You can cut the patch into smaller pieces with scissors if needed to fit the painful area. Wear the patch for up to 12 hours, then take it off and leave your skin uncovered for the next 12 hours (12 hours on, 12 hours off). Wash your hands after touching the patch. Do not put the patch over open wounds, rashes, or irritated skin.
dosing: Use up to 3 patches at one time, applied to the painful area for up to 12 hours within a 24-hour period. Always follow the exact dose your doctor or pharmacist told you. Do not use more patches or wear them longer than directed.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply your patch at the usual time, apply it as soon as you remember. Then remove it after 12 hours as usual and leave the skin bare for the next 12 hours before applying a new patch. Do not apply extra patches to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store patches at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep them in the original sealed envelope until you are ready to use them. Keep all patches out of reach of children and pets. Used patches still contain medicine and must be folded sticky-side together and thrown away safely in the trash, away from children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply the patch to broken, cut, or irritated skin. Do not put the patch near your eyes, mouth, or nose. Do not use a heating pad, electric blanket, or heat lamp over the patch, as heat can increase the amount of medicine absorbed into your body and cause side effects. Avoid swimming or bathing while wearing the patch. Do not wear the patch longer than 12 hours at a time.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical help right away if you experience: severe burning, blistering, or swelling where the patch is applied; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, or throat; dizziness, blurred vision, ringing in the ears, or feeling like you might faint; irregular heartbeat or chest pain; confusion or seizures. Also call your doctor if your pain is not improving after a few weeks of using the patch.
when_it_works: The patch begins to relieve pain within a few hours of putting it on. However, it may take a few days to weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit. The patch helps manage pain while it is on but does not cure the underlying condition.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the medicine in the patch. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this patch if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: This patch is not approved for use in children unless specifically directed by a doctor. Liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as this may affect how your body processes the medicine.
